claim: N-glycans on surface glycoproteins of dendrites shift from immature to mature forms containing sialic acid in response to increased neuronal activation.
source: Here, we observed that N-glycans on surface glycoproteins of dendrites shift from immature to mature forms containing sialic acid in response to increased neuronal activation.
evidence: This is stated as a primary finding in the abstract based on experimental observations.

claim: N-glycosylation alterations result from the growth and proliferation of Golgi satellites scattered throughout the dendrite.
source: In exploring the basis of these N-glycosylation alterations, we discovered that they result from the growth and proliferation of Golgi satellites scattered throughout the dendrite.
evidence: This is stated as a discovery based on experimental exploration.

claim: Golgi satellites that formed during neuronal excitation were in close association with endoplasmic reticulum (ER) exit sites and early endosomes.
source: Golgi satellites that formed during neuronal excitation were in close association with endoplasmic reticulum (ER) exit sites and early endosomes and contained glycosylation machinery without the Golgi structural protein, GM130.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study.

claim: Golgi satellites contain glycosylation machinery without the Golgi structural protein, GM130.
source: Golgi satellites that formed during neuronal excitation were in close association with endoplasmic reticulum (ER) exit sites and early endosomes and contained glycosylation machinery without the Golgi structural protein, GM130.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study.

claim: Golgi satellites function as distal glycosylation stations in dendrites, terminally modifying sugars on newly synthesized glycoproteins passing through the secretory pathway.
source: They functioned as distal glycosylation stations in dendrites, terminally modifying sugars either on newly synthesized glycoproteins passing through the secretory pathway or on surface glycoproteins taken up from the endocytic pathway.
evidence: This is stated as a functional finding from the study.

claim: Golgi satellites terminally modify sugars on surface glycoproteins taken up from the endocytic pathway.
source: They functioned as distal glycosylation stations in dendrites, terminally modifying sugars either on newly synthesized glycoproteins passing through the secretory pathway or on surface glycoproteins taken up from the endocytic pathway.
evidence: This is stated as a functional finding from the study.

claim: Golgi satellite activities led to major changes in the dendritic surface of excited neurons, impacting binding and uptake of lectins.
source: These activities led to major changes in the dendritic surface of excited neurons, impacting binding and uptake of lectins, as well as causing functional changes in neurotransmitter receptors such as nicotinic acetylcholine receptors.
evidence: This is stated as a consequence of Golgi satellite activities based on experimental observations.

claim: Golgi satellite activities cause functional changes in neurotransmitter receptors such as nicotinic acetylcholine receptors.
source: These activities led to major changes in the dendritic surface of excited neurons, impacting binding and uptake of lectins, as well as causing functional changes in neurotransmitter receptors such as nicotinic acetylcholine receptors.
evidence: This is stated as a consequence of Golgi satellite activities based on experimental observations.

claim: Neural activity boosts the activity of the dendrite's satellite micro-secretory system by redistributing Golgi enzymes involved in glycan modifications into peripheral Golgi satellites.
source: Neural activity thus boosts the activity of the dendrite's satellite micro-secretory system by redistributing Golgi enzymes involved in glycan modifications into peripheral Golgi satellites.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the study's findings.

claim: Decentralized protein synthesis in dendrites plays a significant role in protein targeting to remote sites.
source: It is known that decentralized protein synthesis in dendrites plays a significant role in protein targeting to remote sites, with integral membrane and secreted proteins locally processed and trafficked in dendrites through a micro-secretory system (Kennedy and Hanus, 2019).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation to support it.

claim: Newly synthesized proteins move from the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) to ER exit sites (ERESs) scattered across the dendritic ER membrane.
source: Within this system, newly synthesized proteins move from the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) to ER exit sites (ERESs) scattered across the dendritic ER membrane (Aridor et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation to support it.

claim: Newly synthesized proteins are routed to local endosomal compartments before being delivered to the plasma membrane, sidestepping the perinuclear Golgi.
source: The proteins then appear to sidestep the perinuclear Golgi and instead are routed to local endosomal compartments before being delivered to the plasma membrane (Hanus and Ehlers, 2008; Bowen et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations to support it.

claim: The 'Golgi bypass' pathway conveys glycoproteins with predominantly immature sugar chains to the plasma membrane, giving rise to the atypical, 'high-mannose', glycosylation pattern characteristic of dendritic membrane surfaces.
source: This so-called 'Golgi bypass' pathway conveys glycoproteins with predominantly immature sugar chains to the plasma membrane, giving rise to the atypical, 'high-mannose', glycosylation pattern characteristic of dendritic membrane surfaces (Hanus et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation to support it.

claim: The Golgi bypass pathway allows locally synthesized proteins in dendrites to avoid long distance trafficking to and from the perinuclear Golgi apparatus in the soma.
source: A major advantage of the Golgi bypass pathway is that it allows locally synthesized proteins in dendrites to avoid having to undergo long distance trafficking to and from the perinuclear Golgi apparatus in the soma.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the advantage of the Golgi bypass pathway.

claim: Golgi bypass comes at a cost because newly synthesized glycoproteins will no longer be processed by Golgi enzymes, which convert high-mannose sugars on glycoproteins to complex, sialyated forms.
source: Golgi bypass comes at a cost, however, since newly synthesized glycoproteins will no longer be processed by Golgi enzymes, which convert high-mannose sugars on glycoproteins to complex, sialyated forms to expand the glycoprotein's functional repertoire at the plasma membrane.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the disadvantage of the Golgi bypass pathway.

claim: During neuronal excitation, the Golgi apparatus undergoes dispersal from a single perinuclear structure into hundreds of scattered mini-Golgi structures within the soma of cultured neurons.
source: During neuronal excitation, the Golgi apparatus surprisingly undergoes dispersal from a single perinuclear structure into hundreds of scattered mini-Golgi structures within the soma of cultured neurons (Thayer et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation to support it.

claim: Neuronal excitation significantly increases levels of sialic acid on N-linked glycoproteins at dendritic surfaces and their associated synapses.
source: Neuronal excitation also significantly increases levels of sialic acid on N-linked glycoproteins at dendritic surfaces and their associated synapses (Scott and Panin, 2014; Rutishauser, 2008; Boll et al., 2020; Torii et al., 2014), with desialyation of glycoproteins in the brain leading to neuroinflammation, dysmyelination, and cognitive dysfunction (Scott and Panin, 2014; Varki and Gagneux, 2012).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations to support it.

claim: Desialyation of glycoproteins in the brain leads to neuroinflammation, dysmyelination, and cognitive dysfunction.
source: Neuronal excitation also significantly increases levels of sialic acid on N-linked glycoproteins at dendritic surfaces and their associated synapses (Scott and Panin, 2014; Rutishauser, 2008; Boll et al., 2020; Torii et al., 2014), with desialyation of glycoproteins in the brain leading to neuroinflammation, dysmyelination, and cognitive dysfunction (Scott and Panin, 2014; Varki and Gagneux, 2012).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations to support it.

claim: Sialylation of glycoproteins occurs in the Golgi apparatus.
source: Because sialylation of glycoproteins occurs in the Golgi apparatus, we wondered whether the increased sialyation of glycoproteins occurring in excited or stimulated neurons was at all related to the phenomenon of Golgi dispersal seen during neuronal stimulation.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: Membrane excitation in either neurons or non-neuronal cells led to dissolution of the Golgi's compact, centralized appearance, and to the formation of scattered Golgi elements that were adjacent to ERESs as well as endosomes.
source: We found that membrane excitation in either neurons or non-neuronal cells led to dissolution of the Golgi's compact, centralized appearance, and to the formation of scattered Golgi elements that were adjacent to ERESs as well as endosomes.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study.

claim: The disseminated Golgi elements, representing Golgi satellites in dendrites, functioned as part of a micro-secretory/glycosylation system, in which N-glycans attached to either newly synthesized receptors or endocytosed surface receptors were remodeled into complex, sialylated forms.
source: The disseminated Golgi elements, representing Golgi satellites in dendrites, functioned as part of a micro-secretory/glycosylation system, in which N-glycans attached to either newly synthesized receptors or endocytosed surface receptors were remodeled into complex, sialylated forms.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study.

claim: The Golgi-mediated sialyation of glycoproteins had cellular consequences, including increased uptake of the lectin wheat germ agglutinin (WGA).
source: The Golgi-mediated sialyation of glycoproteins had cellular consequences, including increased uptake of the lectin wheat germ agglutinin (WGA) and functional upregulation of specific neurotransmitter receptors.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study.

claim: The Golgi-mediated sialyation of glycoproteins had cellular consequences, including functional upregulation of specific neurotransmitter receptors.
source: The Golgi-mediated sialyation of glycoproteins had cellular consequences, including increased uptake of the lectin wheat germ agglutinin (WGA) and functional upregulation of specific neurotransmitter receptors.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study.

claim: α4β2Rs are the main class of nicotinic receptors with high affinity for nicotine in the brain.
source: In the brain, α4β2Rs are the main class of nicotinic receptors with high affinity for nicotine (Albuquerque et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation to support it.

claim: When α4β2R-expressing HEK293 cells were exposed to 10 µM nicotine, the Golgi dramatically changed from having a compact perinuclear localization to being distributed among discrete smaller elements dispersed throughout the cytoplasm.
source: When α4β2R-expressing HEK293 cells were exposed to 10 µM nicotine, the Golgi dramatically changed from having a compact perinuclear localization to being distributed among discrete smaller elements dispersed throughout the cytoplasm, as observed by localizing exogenously expressed GFP-tagged β-1,4,galactosyltransferase (GalT-GFP), a late-acting Golgi enzyme (Figure 1A, +nicotine).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study and supported by Figure 1A.

claim: Changes in Golgi morphology were initiated within 1 hr of nicotine exposure, lasted as long as nicotine was present, and were reversible with nicotine removal.
source: The changes in Golgi morphology were initiated within 1 hr of nicotine exposure, lasted as long as nicotine was present, and were reversible with nicotine removal (see Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Untreated cells imaged over the same time period showed no Golgi fragmentation, indicating fragmentation was induced by nicotine treatment.
source: Untreated cells imaged over the same time period showed no Golgi fragmentation, indicating fragmentation was induced by nicotine treatment (Figure 1A, -nicotine).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study and supported by Figure 1A.

claim: Golgi dispersal was initiated at nicotine concentrations as low as 300 nM and saturated at ~1 µM nicotine.
source: Golgi dispersal was initiated at nicotine concentrations as low as 300 nM and saturated at ~1 µM nicotine, as shown in cells expressing GalT-GFP and antibody labeling for the Golgi structural marker, GM130 (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study and supported by Figure 1B.

claim: The dose dependence for Golgi fragmentation was similar to the dose dependence for nicotine sensitivity of neurons.
source: The dose dependence for Golgi fragmentation was similar to the dose dependence for nicotine sensitivity of neurons (Vallejo et al., 2005; Govind et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study with citations to support the comparison.

claim: Some Golgi puncta contained all three Golgi markers (GM130, St3, and GalNAc-T2), whereas others had only GalNAc-T2 or St3-GFP associated with them and no GM130 labeling.
source: We found that some Golgi puncta contained all three Golgi markers, whereas others had only GalNAc-T2 or St3-GFP associated with them and no GM130 labeling (Figure 1C, see arrows in zoomed boxes).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study and supported by Figure 1C.

claim: The numbers of Golgi puncta containing only GalNAc-T2 or St3-GFP without GM130 were significantly increased by nicotine exposure.
source: The numbers of these puncta were significantly increased by nicotine exposure (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study and supported by Figure 1D.

claim: No change in Golgi morphology was observed in HEK293 cells not expressing α4β2Rs after overnight nicotine treatment, indicating α4β2R expression was required for nicotine-dependent Golgi dispersal.
source: No change in Golgi morphology was observed in HEK293 cells not expressing α4β2Rs after overnight nicotine treatment (Figure 1E), indicating α4β2R expression was required for nicotine-dependent Golgi dispersal.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study and supported by Figure 1E.

claim: Golgi outposts are enriched in GM130 and other Golgi enzymes, and usually localize only to the most proximal part of the apical dendrite or at dendrite branch points.
source: These structures are enriched in GM130 and other Golgi enzymes, and usually localize only to the most proximal part of the apical dendrite or at dendrite branch points (Horton and Ehlers, 2003).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation to support it.

claim: Golgi satellites are usually smaller than Golgi outposts and are widely dispersed in dendrites.
source: These structures are usually smaller than Golgi outposts and are widely dispersed in dendrites.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about Golgi satellites.

claim: Golgi satellites lack GM130 and contain glycosylation machinery.
source: Golgi satellites lack GM130 and contain glycosylation machinery (Mikhaylova et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation to support it.

claim: Golgi satellites have been shown to be near ERESs as well as recycling endosomes, and thus could contribute to the micro-secretory system occurring in dendrites.
source: They have been shown to be near ERESs as well as recycling endosomes, and thus could contribute to the micro-secretory system occurring in dendrites (Mikhaylova et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation to support it, with speculation about their contribution.

claim: Within cultured neurons from rat cortex, 5–10% of neurons are endogenously expressing α4β2Rs, with their expression largely found in inhibitory neurons.
source: Within these cultures, 5–10% of neurons are endogenously expressing α4β2Rs, with their expression largely found in inhibitory neurons (Govind et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation to support it.

claim: Nicotine treatment caused Golgi structures to fragment into scattered elements in the cell body of neurons expressing α4β2Rs.
source: Examining the cell body of these neurons revealed that nicotine treatment caused Golgi structures to fragment into scattered elements (Figure 2Ai–Ci; see boxed areas in images labeled with the different Golgi markers and their corresponding enlarged images).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study and supported by Figure 2Ai–Ci.

claim: Large Golgi puncta contained all of the different Golgi markers, whereas small Golgi structures contained mainly Golgi enzymes (i.e., St3, GalNAc-T2, and Man II) without GM130.
source: Large Golgi puncta contained all of the different Golgi markers, whereas small Golgi structures contained mainly Golgi enzymes (i.e., St3, GalNAc-T2, and Man II) without GM130 (Figure 2Ai–Ci).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study and supported by Figure 2Ai–Ci.

claim: In neurons with low electrical activity, there are normally relatively few dendritic Golgi satellites.
source: In neurons with low electrical activity, we found that there are normally relatively few dendritic Golgi satellites.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study.

claim: Nicotine treatment did not change the low number of GM130-positive Golgi outposts.
source: Nicotine treatment did not change the low number of GM130-positive Golgi outposts; however, the GM130-negative Golgi satellite structures containing GalNAc-T2, St3, and/or Man II underwent a significant increase in number in response to nicotine treatment (Figure 2Aii–Cii).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study and supported by Figure 2Aii–Cii.

claim: The GM130-negative Golgi satellite structures containing GalNAc-T2, St3, and/or Man II underwent a significant increase in number in response to nicotine treatment.
source: Nicotine treatment did not change the low number of GM130-positive Golgi outposts; however, the GM130-negative Golgi satellite structures containing GalNAc-T2, St3, and/or Man II underwent a significant increase in number in response to nicotine treatment (Figure 2Aii–Cii).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study and supported by Figure 2Aii–Cii.

claim: An increase in the number and density of St3-containing puncta per dendrite length was observed for both bicuculline treatment and APV withdrawal compared to vehicle control or chronic APV treatment.
source: An increase in the number and density of St3-containing puncta per dendrite length was observed for both treatments compared to vehicle control or chronic APV treatment (Figure 2F–H).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study and supported by Figure 2F–H.

claim: Changes in neuronal activity alone are sufficient to drive the formation of enzyme-rich Golgi satellites in soma and dendritic processes of neurons.
source: We thus concluded that changes in neuronal activity alone are sufficient to drive the formation of enzyme-rich Golgi satellites in soma and dendritic processes of neurons.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the study's findings.

claim: RUSH-mApple-GPI could be seen quickly passing through St3-GFP-labeled Golgi fragments before arriving at the plasma membrane in time lapse sequences.
source: RUSH-mApple-GPI could be seen quickly passing through St3-GFP-labeled Golgi fragments before arriving at the plasma membrane in time lapse sequences.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study.

claim: The kinetics of RUSH-mApple-GPI trafficking in nicotine-treated cells resembled that for RUSH-mApple-GPI in cells not treated with nicotine.
source: The kinetics of this trafficking resembled that for RUSH-mApple-GPI in cells not treated with nicotine (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study and supported by Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Dispersed Golgi elements in nicotine-treated cells behave as bona fide units of the secretory pathway.
source: Thus, dispersed Golgi elements in nicotine-treated cells behave as bona fide units of the secretory pathway.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the study's findings.

claim: Upon addition of the membrane-permeable ligand, the aggregates of ESCargo disassembled, resulting in soluble ESCargo rapidly filling the ER lumen due to its increased ability to diffuse.
source: Upon addition of the membrane-permeable ligand, the aggregates of ESCargo disassembled, resulting in soluble ESCargo rapidly filling the ER lumen due to its increased ability to diffuse (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study and supported by Figure 3C.

claim: After ESCargo release, the cargo moved out of the ER into non-motile Man II-containing Golgi puncta distributed along the dendrites.
source: Thereafter, the cargo moved out of the ER into non-motile Man II-containing Golgi puncta distributed along the dendrites.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study.

claim: The intensity of ESCargo in many Golgi puncta could be seen to subsequently diminish, consistent with the cargo's downstream trafficking and delivery to the plasma membrane.
source: The intensity of ESCargo in many Golgi puncta could be seen to subsequently diminish, consistent with the cargo's downstream trafficking and delivery to the plasma membrane.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study with an interpretation.

claim: Newly synthesized proteins traffic from the ER through dispersed Golgi satellites en route to the plasma membrane in stimulated neurons.
source: These data provide evidence that newly synthesized proteins traffic from the ER through dispersed Golgi satellites en route to the plasma membrane in stimulated neurons.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the study's findings.

claim: St3-GFP-labeled Golgi puncta were often found to reside next to mCh-Sec23 structures in dendrites of nicotine-treated neurons.
source: St3-GFP-labeled Golgi puncta were often found to reside next to mCh-Sec23 structures in dendrites of nicotine-treated neurons (Figure 4A, see arrows).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study and supported by Figure 4A.

claim: A line scan analysis revealed that the peak intensity of St3-labeled Golgi puncta was ~300 nm from the peak intensity of ERESs marked by Sec23.
source: A line scan analysis across the boxed structure in Figure 4A revealed that the peak intensity of St3-labeled Golgi puncta was ~300 nm from the peak intensity of ERESs marked by Sec23 (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study and supported by Figure 4B.

claim: Dendritic Golgi satellites in nicotine-treated neurons were adjacent to early endosomes labeled with the early endosomal marker EEA1.
source: Dendritic Golgi satellites in nicotine-treated neurons were also adjacent to early endosomes labeled with the early endosomal marker EEA1 (Figure 4C, see arrows), with an individual Golgi satellite and endosome within 300 nm of each other's center (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study and supported by Figure 4C and 4D.

claim: The number of Golgi satellites closely associated with endosomes was increased by neuronal stimulation.
source: The number of Golgi satellites closely associated with endosomes was increased by neuronal stimulation (see Figure 8E,F).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study and supported by Figure 8E,F.

claim: Many Golgi satellites resided adjacent to both Sec23-labeled and EEA1-labeled puncta.
source: In triple-labeling experiments, in which neurons were transfected with St3-GFP and mCh-Sec23 and then labeled with antibodies to EEA1, we found that many Golgi satellites resided adjacent to both Sec23-labeled and EEA1-labeled puncta (Figure 4E and F).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study and supported by Figure 4E and F.

claim: Dendritic Golgi satellites often situate themselves next to sites of ER export and early endosomes, similar to what has been reported for dendritic Golgi satellites in untreated neurons.
source: Thus, dendritic Golgi satellites often situate themselves next to sites of ER export and early endosomes, similar to what has been reported for dendritic Golgi satellites in untreated neurons (Mikhaylova et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the study's findings with a citation to support the comparison.

claim: When microtubules are depolymerized by nocodazole treatment, Golgi enzymes are relocated to ERESs that are still functional for secretory transport.
source: When microtubules are depolymerized by nocodazole treatment, Golgi enzymes are relocated to ERESs that are still functional for secretory transport (Cole et al., 1996).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation to support it.

claim: Golgi fragments induced by either nicotine or nocodazole treatment in non-neuronal cells expressing α4β2Rs had similar size ranges and contents.
source: Golgi fragments induced by either nicotine or nocodazole treatment in non-neuronal cells expressing α4β2Rs had similar size ranges and contents, with some fragments containing both St3 and GM130 (usually larger ones) and others having only St3 (often small ones) (Figure 5A and B; Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study and supported by Figure 5A and B; Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Golgi fragmentation induced by either nicotine or nocodazole treatment was reversible upon drug removal.
source: In addition, Golgi fragmentation induced by either treatment was reversible upon drug removal (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Microtubules remained intact when either α4β2R-expressing HEK293 cells or neurons were treated with nicotine, unlike that observed when microtubules were depolymerized with nocodazole.
source: Despite these similarities, microtubules (visualized using the microtubule binding protein ensconsin) remained intact when either α4β2R-expressing HEK293 cells or neurons were treated with nicotine, unlike that observed when microtubules were depolymerized with nocodazole (Figure 5C–E).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study and supported by Figure 5C–E.

claim: Golgi fragmentation in nicotine-treated cells, while sharing similarities to Golgi fragmentation in nocodazole-treated cells, was not due to microtubules being disrupted.
source: This suggested that Golgi fragmentation in nicotine-treated cells, while sharing similarities to Golgi fragmentation in nocodazole-treated cells, was not due to microtubules being disrupted.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the study's findings.

claim: Within 17 hr of nicotine treatment, the majority of α4 subunits associated with surface-labeled α4β2Rs had shifted to a higher molecular weight form.
source: As can be seen in Figure 6A, after 17 hr of nicotine treatment, the majority of α4 subunits associated with surface-labeled α4β2Rs had shifted to a higher molecular weight form.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study and supported by Figure 6A.

claim: The α4 subunits could be cleaved to lower molecular, nonglycosylated forms by the glycan-specific cleavage reagents Endo H or PNGase F.
source: The α4 subunits could be cleaved to lower molecular, nonglycosylated forms by the glycan-specific cleavage reagents Endo H or PNGase F (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study and supported by Figure 6A.

claim: No shift in molecular weight of surface-labeled α4β2Rs was seen in untreated cells.
source: No such shift in molecular weight of surface-labeled α4β2Rs was seen in untreated cells.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study.

claim: Incubating cells with swainsonine, a drug that prevents N-glycans on proteins from being converted from high mannose to complex forms, prevented the molecular weight shift in α4 subunits during nicotine treatment.
source: Incubating cells with swainsonine, a drug that prevents N-glycans on proteins from being converted from high mannose to complex forms, prevented the molecular weight shift in α4 subunits during nicotine treatment (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study and supported by Figure 6B.

claim: The glycans on α4 subunits of α4β2Rs in nicotine-treated cells were sensitive to neuraminidase, an enzyme that cleaves off sialic acid from glycans.
source: Further analysis of the sugar modifications on α4 subunits of α4β2Rs in nicotine-treated cells revealed that they were sensitive to neuraminidase (Figure 6C), an enzyme that cleaves off sialic acid from glycans.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study and supported by Figure 6C.

claim: α4 subunits could be precipitated by the sialic acid binding lectin SNA, confirming the glycans on α4 subunits contained sialic acid.
source: In addition, α4 subunits could be precipitated by the sialic acid binding lectin SNA (Figure 6D), confirming the glycans on α4 subunits contained sialic acid.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study and supported by Figure 6D.

claim: The increase in the molecular weight of α4 subunits from sialic acid addition was blocked by ammonium chloride treatment, which increases pH within intracellular organelles.
source: The increase in the molecular weight of α4 subunits from sialic acid addition was blocked by ammonium chloride treatment, which increases pH within intracellular organelles (Figure 6E), raising the possibility that low pH-requiring Golgi sialotransferases St3 and/or St6 were involved in the sialic acid addition (Rivinoja et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study and supported by Figure 6E, with speculation about the mechanism.

claim: Within 2 hr of nicotine treatment, α4 subunits associated with α4β2Rs at the cell surface had begun to display complex glycan forms.
source: Within 2 hr of nicotine treatment, α4 subunits associated with α4β2Rs at the cell surface had begun to display complex glycan forms (Figure 6F), with the kinetics of this process (Figure 6G) resembling the timing of Golgi dispersal in these cells (see Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study and supported by Figure 6F and 6G.

claim: The kinetics of α4 subunit glycan conversion resembled the timing of Golgi dispersal in nicotine-treated cells.
source: Within 2 hr of nicotine treatment, α4 subunits associated with α4β2Rs at the cell surface had begun to display complex glycan forms (Figure 6F), with the kinetics of this process (Figure 6G) resembling the timing of Golgi dispersal in these cells (see Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study and supported by Figure 6F, 6G, and 1A.

claim: N-glycans on surface α4β2Rs change from being immature types to mature types containing sialic acid in nicotine-treated cells, with conversion likely occurring as α4β2Rs traffic through dispersed Golgi elements.
source: Collectively, these data indicate that N-glycans on surface α4β2Rs change from being immature types to mature types containing sialic acid in nicotine-treated cells, with conversion likely occurring as α4β2Rs traffic through dispersed Golgi elements.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the study's findings.

claim: Significant overlap between endocytosed HA antibody-labeled α4β2Rs and small Golgi puncta in somata and dendrites could be seen, with seemingly greater internalization and Golgi delivery under nicotine treatment.
source: After this treatment, significant overlap between endocytosed HA antibody-labeled α4β2Rs and small Golgi puncta in somata and dendrites could be seen, with seemingly greater internalization and Golgi delivery under nicotine treatment (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study and supported by Figure 7A.

claim: In dendrites, the number of Golgi fragments containing HA antibodies to α4β2Rs increased threefold after nicotine treatment.
source: In dendrites, where overlap was easier to quantify, the number of Golgi fragments containing HA antibodies to α4β2Rs increased threefold after nicotine treatment (Figure 7B and C).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study and supported by Figure 7B and C.

claim: Endocytosed α4β2Rs co-localized with EEA1-labeled endosomes and this co-localization increased with nicotine treatment.
source: We also found that endocytosed α4β2Rs co-localized with EEA1-labeled endosomes and that this co-localization increased with nicotine treatment (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study and supported by Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: Endocytosed α4β2Rs can be delivered to Golgi satellites and nicotine treatment increases this process.
source: These results demonstrate that endocytosed α4β2Rs can be delivered to Golgi satellites and that nicotine treatment increases this process.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the study's findings.

claim: Within 2 hr after surface biotinylation and continuing thereafter, the glycans on α4 subunits in nicotine-treated cells had begun being converted to higher molecular weight, complex forms.
source: We found that within 2 hr after surface biotinylation and continuing thereafter, the glycans on α4 subunits in nicotine-treated cells had begun being converted to higher molecular weight, complex forms (Figure 7D), consistent with their having been delivered to Golgi fragments from the cell surface.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study and supported by Figure 7D.

claim: No conversion of α4 subunit glycans was seen in untreated cells.
source: No such conversion was seen in untreated cells.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study.

claim: The 'protected' (i.e., internalized) pool of biotinylated α4 in nicotine-treated cells increased over time and by 2 hr consisted of α4 subunits with complex-type glycans of increased molecular weight.
source: As shown in Figure 7E, the 'protected' (i.e., internalized) pool of biotinylated α4 (i.e., internalized) in nicotine-treated cells increased over time and by 2 hr consisted of α4 subunits with complex-type glycans of increased molecular weight.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study and supported by Figure 7E.

claim: Nicotine appears to stimulate surface α4β2Rs to traffic to Golgi satellites in HEK293 cells, where their N-glycans are modified to higher molecular weight, complex forms.
source: Therefore, nicotine appears to stimulate surface α4β2Rs to traffic to Golgi satellites in HEK293 cells, where their N-glycans are modified to higher molecular weight, complex forms.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the study's findings.

claim: HEK293 cells expressing α4β2Rs showed significantly enhanced ACh-evoked currents after nicotine treatment.
source: The expressing cells showed significantly enhanced ACh-evoked currents after nicotine treatment (Figure 7F and G, control).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study and supported by Figure 7F and G.

claim: The enhancement of ACh-evoked currents after nicotine treatment was markedly reduced by swainsonine treatment without impacting the low level currents under no nicotine treatment.
source: Notably, this enhancement was markedly reduced by swainsonine treatment without impacting the low level currents under no nicotine treatment (Figure 7F and G, swainsonine).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study and supported by Figure 7F and G.

claim: Overall levels of surface α4β2Rs did not change during swainsonine treatment.
source: Other experiments showed that overall levels of surface α4β2Rs did not change during swainsonine treatment (Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study and supported by Figure 7—figure supplement 2.
